items.title: Trade Desk Falls 4% on 15% Workforce Cut; AppLovin Ascends 3%, Magnite Pulls Back
items.summary: The Trade Desk just announced a sweeping workforce cut and a parade of executive replacements, while rivals AppLovin and Magnite pull further ahead. Whether this signals a genuine strategic reset or a company quietly shrinking to survive is the question investors are now pricing in real time.

items.title: Is AppLovin Stock Priced For A Sharper Slowdown Than Management Guides To?
items.summary: AppLovin (APP) has fallen about 43.9% over the trailing three months and sits roughly 57% below its 52-week high, at about $313.58 a share. Even after a drop that size, the advertising platform is priced at about 23.2 times its trailing adjusted earnings. That figure is on every screen, and it is the one that tells you least about what you are buying.

items.title: AppLovin (APP) Down 6.6% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Rebound?
items.summary: AppLovin (APP) reported earnings 30 days ago. What's next for the stock? We take a look at earnings estimates for some clues.

items.title: How Much Upside Can APP Stock's Growth Deliver?
items.summary: While known for gaming, the company's fastest growth is happening elsewhere. Its consumer vertical is quietly becoming a second engine, with advertiser spend already setting records. This segment finished the second quarter 28% above fourth quarter 2025 levels.

items.title: Can AppLovin's 53% Revenue Surge Keep Its Growth Streak Alive?
items.summary: APP's 53% revenue surge, record margins and Q3 outlook extend its growth streak, but sustaining advertiser demand is key to keeping momentum alive.

items.title: AppLovin Stock: Is APP Underperforming the Communication Services Sector?
items.summary: AppLovin has notably underperformed the Communication Services sector over the past year, but analysts are highly optimistic about the stock’s prospects.

items.title: AppLovin’s Algorithmic Moat Is Vulnerable, Says Investor: Why $1.9B Quarterly Revenue Isn’t Enough to Justify a Buy
items.summary: AppLovin prints $1.9 billion quarters and 84% margins, yet two disciplined investors studied the model and walked away. Their reason cuts to the heart of what separates a durable moat from a very good algorithm.

items.title: 3 Founder Backed Growth Stocks To Watch In September 2026
items.summary: Government bond yields in many major economies are at multi year highs, which indicates that central banks are serious about keeping inflation in check. Higher yields can pressure some stocks, but they also push investors to look more closely at companies with solid growth plans and leaders who have real money at stake.
